text:
maya: Heads up — seeing a spike of GPU node provisioning failures in ap-southeast-1 since ~00:12 UTC. Nodes stall at `attach-keystore` and then timeout.

maya: Example from node-az2-gtx: `ERROR: keystore decrypt failed: AccessDenied: user does not have kms:Decrypt on arn:aws:kms:ap-southeast-1:...:key/abcd-ef01`

raj: uhh — did anyone push KMS policy changes or cross-account grants in the quiet window? @security-bot? :eyes:

security-bot: We rotated a couple customer-facing keystore keys during the 00:05–00:10 maintenance window. Policy change note: removed `kms:Decrypt` wildcard from compute role while we tightened key usage constraints.

leila: That lines up. I pushed the firewall segmentation rule to tighten mgmt-plane access at 00:07 (segmented subnets -> deny inbound from shared-control). Could be related if node bootstrap talks to a keystore endpoint in a different subnet.

maya: I can repro locally by creating a test instance with the same instance profile — it can't reach the KMS endpoint due to the new subnet route. Logs show `Endpoint unreachable` followed by `AccessDenied` as a fallback.

samir: Two potential knock-on effects: 1) nodes failing to get keys will fallback to disk-encrypted path and then fail provisioning -> capacity shortfall, 2) fallback routing is sending traffic via cross-region NAT which spikes egress cost for that AZ.

maya: Confirmed — temporary fallback sent requests to eu-west-1 NAT and we saw ~$1.2K egress in the last hour on staging billing. Not huge but will escalate if prod follows.

raj: Immediate mitigation options: A) roll back the mgmt-plane subnet rule to allow control-plane -> keystore endpoint, B) add a VPC endpoint / policy exception for the keystore service, or C) re-grant kms:Decrypt to the instance profile while we sort routing. Preferences?

leila: Option B is lowest-risk — create a VPC endpoint for KMS and add policy allowing our instance role. But that requires infra change and verification, might take 20–30m.

security-bot: We can temporarily add a scoped `kms:Decrypt` exception for the instance role but must log and expire it in 30 minutes. I can author a short auditable change.

ops-bot: Canary capacity alert: GPU pool ap-southeast-1/GPU-PROD going from 98% -> 65% ready nodes; pending queue increasing.

samir: Ok do both B and temporary scoped exception. leila -- can you open the VPC endpoint PR? I’ll coordinate the scoped exception with security and flip it off after verification.

leila: On it. PR branch: `infra/kms-vpce-ap-segmentation-2321`. Will link shortly.

security-bot: Scoped exception prepared: policy snippet below. Will apply once leila posts VPCE ID. Expires in 30m after apply.

security-bot: ```json
{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/gpu-instance-role"},"Action":["kms:Decrypt"],"Resource":"arn:aws:kms:ap-southeast-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01","Condition":{"DateLessThan":{"aws:CurrentTime":"2023-12-31T00:30:00Z"}}}]}
```

maya: After applying the exception we saw node boot success rate go from 42% -> 96% within 4 minutes. Monitoring tail looks good.

raj: Nice. After VPCE is up and tested let's remove the exception and confirm audits show only that one temporary grant. Security, mark this as high-sensitivity change and add to incident tracker.

security-bot: Noted. Creating incident record and attaching VPC endpoint PR and the temporary policy change.

samir: Follow-ups: 1) Add an automated preflight that runs keystore reachability checks when mgmt-plane subnet rules change, 2) Add cost guardrail to detect unexpected cross-region egress from fallback routes, 3) Update runbook to prefer VPCE for KMS access in segmented-net designs. Assigned: samir (preflight), leila (VPCE PR + runbook), maya (monitoring/alerts), raj (cost guardrail).

leila: PR link: https://git.internal/repo/infra/pulls/452 — contains route changes and VPCE creation.

maya: I'll keep monitoring and will post status in 30m. Thanks all :thumbsup:

raj: Closing loop: once exception removed and VPCE verified, post snippet of audit log (kms:Decrypt events) so we can confirm no lingering grants.

maya: Will do. End state: nodes healthy, VPCE in place, temporary grant revoked, incident filed.
